chunks: And by this chain from Salih ibn al-Harith ibn al-Mughira from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has angels assigned to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). When a man intends to visit it, He gives them his sins; when he takes a step, He erases them, and when he takes another step, He multiplies his good deeds. His good deeds continue to be multiplied until they secure Paradise for him.
Then they surround him and sanctify him.
And they call upon the angels of the sky, saying: 'Sanctify the visitors to the grave of the beloved of the beloved of Allah.'
When they have performed the ritual bath, Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) calls out to them: 'O guests of Allah, receive glad tidings of accompanying me in Paradise.'
Then the Commander of the Faithful, Ali (peace be upon him), calls out to them: 'I am the guarantor for your needs and the removal of calamity from you in this world and the hereafter.'
Then they surround them on their right and on their left until they return to their families.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic interactions for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the unique intercessory role of angels and the Ahl al-Bayt in the spiritual economy of Ziyarat, emphasizing that the physical act of approaching the grave triggers a divine mechanism of sin erasure and deed multiplication. It underscores the Shia belief in the continuity of spiritual guardianship, where Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali actively guarantee the visitor’s worldly needs and otherworldly safety, framing the pilgrimage as a holistic journey of purification and divine favor.
